notes: AR(1) rho=0.5 LD; n_causal=3-10 planted; estimate_prior_method='optim'; max_iter=100; tol=1e-6. Observed-then-floored measurement.
ceiling_note: At p>=1000 the per-outer-iter ELBO call (torch.linalg.solve on R, O(p^3)) dominates both paths equally; the kernel itself is fast but represents <10% of total fit_rss time. Caching the Cholesky factorisation of R across IBSS iterations is a separate Python-side optimisation that would unlock the C++ savings at biobank scale.
kernel_only_speedup: On the work the kernel replaces (per-layer SER + Brent V optimiser + softmax + EM), profiled at p=500 the kernel runs in 17ms vs 110ms Python (6.5x). The headline speedup degrades at large p because of the unchanged ELBO.
